 Live .  58,740 viewing 58740 viewing Live page Updated 3 minutes ago Russell Brand found guilty of rape and three sexual assaults
 Summary
 Warning: This page contains distressing details 
 Russell Brand has been found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault - read a summary of his offences here 
 The judge tells him "obviously a custodial sentence of some length will result" 
 The comedian and actor, 51, has been remanded in custody and will be sentenced on Monday
 Brand faced seven charges: three of rape, three of sexual assault and one of attempted indecent assault. He was found not guilty on three counts 
 The seven charges dated from 1999 to 2009 and concerned six women. They are all entitled to lifelong anonymity
 It can now be reported that Brand is being investigated over further rape allegations made by two women 
 Media caption, Watch: Met Police interview Brand in 2025 Live Reporting
 Edited by Owen Amos and Alex Smith, with Helena Wilkinson and Sima Kotecha in Southwark Crown Court
 Channel 4 says it recognises 'profound impact' of Brand's crimes published at 16:25 GMT 16:25 GMT 
 Among the four offences Brand has been found guilty of is a sexual assault charge while working on a Channel 4 project in 2009.
 He laid his head into the groin area of a woman working with him at the time without her consent.
 In a statement, the broadcaster says: "Our thoughts are first and foremost with the six women involved in the case against Russell Brand, including those affected by the crimes for which he has been convicted. 
 "We recognise the profound impact of these crimes and commend the extraordinary courage of all those who gave evidence as prosecution witnesses at trial."

 Photographers wait for Brand to leave in prison van published at 16:08 GMT 16:08 GMT 
 Helena Wilkinson 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 Outside Southwark Crown Court, dozens of photographers and journalists are waiting by a gate to the side of the building for the prison van to leave. 
 Inside it will be Russell Brand.
 Each morning and afternoon during his trial, Brand walked into and out of Southwark Crown Court with his entourage, including his wife Laura.
 But this afternoon they left without him. 
 Soon, the man who was one of most in-demand entertainers, will be heading to prison to spend his first night there, ahead of his sentencing on Monday. 
 Image source, EPA Image caption, Journalists listening to statements from the police and CPS earlier today

 Video shows police officers interviewing Brand in 2025 published at 15:58 GMT 15:58 GMT Breaking 
 The Metropolitan Police has released footage of officers interviewing Brand in July 2025 - watch a section below.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 You've looked beautiful in court, Brand told wife in podcast during trial published at 15:54 GMT 15:54 GMT 
 Helena Wilkinson and Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 Before and during Brand's rape and sexual assault trial, videos were posted on his social media accounts to his millions of followers.
 In one episode called "The I of The Storm", Brand talked about feeling "God's presence" walking into court.
 The day after the prosecution opened the case to the jury, a post on Brand's X account said "the prayer is working thank you".
 And at the end of the first week of his trial another episode called "Sunday Service with the Brands" was posted.
 "You've looked absolutely beautiful and spectacular," Brand told his wife, referring to what she had worn to court.
 "You've looked wonderful too," she replied.
 Laura Brand said they read psalms on their way to court and before they went in they prayed.
 Referring to media covering the trial, she said: "We are pretty vigilant about not engaging in the media around it, it's too evil, sorry to say."
 Image source, EPA Image caption, Russell and Laura Brand arriving at court earlier today

 Images of police interviews released published at 15:38 GMT 15:38 GMT 
 We can now bring you images from some of Russell Brand's police interviews, issued by the Metropolitan Police.
 The first dates from 2025; the second from 2023.
 Image source, PA / Met Police Image caption, A CCTV image issued by Metropolitan Police of a police interview with Russell Brand in July 2025
 Image source, PA / Met Police Image caption, This image is of a police interview in November 2023

 Brand was found not guilty of three offences published at 15:27 GMT 15:27 GMT 
 Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 Russell Brand faced seven charges in total: three of rape, three of sexual assault and one of attempted indecent assault. 
 He was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault - you can read a summary of his offences here. 
 He was found not guilty on three counts.
 Brand was cleared of raping a woman at a hotel in Bournemouth in 1999, where he was attending the Labour Party conference. He had been performing at a cabaret show where he met the woman.
He was found not guilty of an attempted indecent assault offence - he was accused of grabbing a woman’s arm and pulling her towards a toilet in 2001.
 He was also found not guilty of orally raping a woman in a toilet at a bar in London. The attack was alleged to have happened when they had been at a birthday party together.

 Police giving statements outside court - watch live published at 15:14 GMT 15:14 GMT 
 Image source, PA Media Police are now giving statements outside Southwark Crown Court following the guilty verdicts.
 You can watch live at the top of the page.

 'At the centre of every assault was an abuse of power' - prosecutor published at 15:13 GMT 15:13 GMT 
 We can now bring you a statement from the Crown Prosecution Service.
 "Russell Brand was predatory and used his celebrity status to commit sexual crimes," says David Roberts, senior prosecutor in the London rape and serious sexual assault unit.
 "He was a manipulator with an insatiable desire to get what he wanted regardless of whether consent was given or not.
 "As his career took off, he seized opportunities to assault the women around him.
 "Although his tactics varied, at the centre of every assault was an abuse of power and sexual greed, with a complete disregard for the impact of his actions.
 "I would like to thank all the women in this case for their courage in coming forward and seeing this sexual abuser brought to justice."
 Image source, Getty Images

 Brand's attitude to women 'absolutely deplorable', says former colleague published at 15:07 GMT 15:07 GMT Breaking 
 Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 A comedian and writer who worked with Russell Brand has described him as being "like a wolf" where women were concerned.
 Cole Parker shared an agent with Brand in the 1990s, and the two men often performed on the same comedy circuit. He says they were in contact until 2013.
 In an interview with the BBC, Parker says Brand’s attitude towards women was "absolutely deplorable", and that he would often go from being "very charming to very angry and threatening when he didn't get what he wanted".
 "If a girl walked past him, he'd give himself whiplash, looking at her so quickly. He would stare at women the way that a starving person would stare at a plate of food.
 "He looked like a wolf. He looked like he was about to jump on them."
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Brand's father tells BBC: 'I just didn't expect this - it's wrong' published at 15:05 GMT 15:05 GMT 
 Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 Ron Brand, Russell’s father, tells the BBC he’s "bemused and shocked" by the verdicts.
 "I just didn’t expect this - it’s wrong," he says. "It’s devastating."

 'I'm good, I'm good' - Brand mouths to defence counsel after verdict published at 15:02 GMT 15:02 GMT 
 Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 Image source, Elizabeth Cook/Press Association After the verdict, Russell Brand returns to the dock to hear details of his sentencing hearing, which will take place on Monday. 
 Brand is sitting down, his wife is absent from the public gallery.
 For what I think is the first time during this trial, the door to the dock is closed.
 The judge thanks the defence for submissions and confirms we’ll meet again on Monday at 10:30 GMT for sentencing.
 Brand exits the dock and is remanded in custody - he’s refused bail.
 As he leaves the dock, he mouths "I'm good, I'm good" to his defence counsel.
 His walk was steady paced and he continued to show little emotion.

 One count of rape and three counts of sexual assault - a summary of Brand's convictions published at 14:55 GMT 14:55 GMT 
 Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 Warning: This post contains distressing details 
 As a reminder, Russell Brand has been found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. 
 The comedian and actor has been found guilty of sexually assaulting a woman at a bar in London in 2004.
 They’d been at a birthday party in Soho and had been chatting at the bar for less than a minute when Brand grabbed her breasts.
 He has been found guilty of sexually assaulting a woman at the Choice FM studios in London in either 2004 or 2005. He grabbed her face and kissed her before touching her breasts and bottom.
 Brand has also been found guilty of raping a woman at his then home in London in 2009, days after meeting her at the Hammersmith Apollo theatre where he’d been performing a comedy show.
 She visited his home in Hampstead where they had consensual sex before he anally raped her. She had told the court “he hurt me and harmed me and when I asked him to stop he didn’t”.
 Brand has also been found guilty of a sexual assault charge while working on a Channel 4 project in 2009.
 The 51-year-old laid his head into the groin area of a woman working with him at the time without her consent.
 The woman said his mouth and nose were in her vaginal area. She told the court she was repulsed at the situation and reported the incident to her line manager at the time.

 'As Brand's profile grew, so too did his sense of entitlement' - police published at 14:50 GMT 14:50 GMT 
 Image source, PA Media We can now bring you reaction from the Metropolitan Police.
 "Today's verdict is first and foremost a testament to the extraordinary courage, resilience and determination of the women who came forward and reported what happened to them," Det Supt Andy Furphy says.
 "Despite intense media and public scrutiny, they relived deeply personal and traumatic experiences and placed their trust in us. Without their bravery, this outcome would not have been possible.
 "Brand used his influence, status and fame to exploit and sexually offend against women. 
 "As his profile grew, so too did his sense of entitlement. I hope this conviction sends a clear message that no one is above the law, no matter how famous or powerful they may be. 
 "I want to pay tribute to the team of detectives and specialist staff who worked tirelessly on this investigation. Their professionalism, determination and compassion for the victims represent the very best of the Metropolitan Police. 
 "Finally, I would urge anyone who may have been a victim of rape or serious sexual assault to speak to us.
 "You will be listened to, supported, and treated with dignity and respect."

 Brand showed no emotion as guilty verdicts read out published at 14:43 GMT 14:43 GMT 
 Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 Image source, Elizabeth Cook/Press Association The court was incredibly quiet as the verdicts were read out.
 Brand looked to the ceiling just before he heard the voice of the jury foreman.
 His wife looked pink in the face as she watched on from the public gallery. A woman held her hand tightly.
 As the guilty verdicts were read out, Laura Brand appeared to blink. Her husband continued to be incredibly still and appeared to show no emotion.
 He closed his eyes when the guilty rape verdict was delivered.

 Brand being investigated over more rape allegations published at 14:36 GMT 14:36 GMT Breaking 
 Helena Wilkinson and Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 Russell Brand is being investigated over further rape allegations made by two women, it can now be reported.
 It’s also emerged that Brand, 51, has already been questioned by officers in relation to the complaints.
 The Metropolitan Police said its investigation into the allegations "remains ongoing".
 In a statement the force said: "The suspect has previously been interviewed under caution in connection with the allegations."
 It said that files had been submitted to the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) in relation to both complainants.
 "Detectives remain in close contact with prosecutors as enquiries continue and further investigative work is carried out," the force added.
 Officers also encouraged anyone wishing to speak to detectives or make a report to contact them.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Brand to be remanded in custody published at 14:26 GMT 14:26 GMT Breaking 
 More now from the judge. 
 Mr Justice Bennathan says: "You’ve been convicted of a number of offences including rape.
 "The consequence of that is inevitably a significant custodial term.
 "My current view is that I therefore have to remand you into custody."
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Judge says Brand should expect jail published at 14:24 GMT 14:24 GMT Breaking 
 Image source, Elizabeth Cook/Press Association Speaking after the verdict is delivered, judge Mr Justice Bennathan says: "Sit down Mr Brand."
 He adds that "given the verdict on count six at least, obviously a custodial sentence of some length will result".
 The judge says the case was "very well prepared", adding the sentencing hearing will take place on Monday.

 Brand found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault published at 14:17 GMT 14:17 GMT Breaking 
 Russell Brand has been found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.
 This is a breaking news story, we'll bring you more details shortly.

 Packed courtroom as Brand awaits verdict published at 14:13 GMT 14:13 GMT 
 Helena Wilkinson 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 The courtroom is packed.
 Russell Brand is in the dock sitting down. Two security officers are also in the dock with him.
 Brand's wife Laura is in the public gallery. A woman next to her is holding her hand. 
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 What has the trial heard so far? published at 14:12 GMT 14:12 GMT 
 Image source, Julia Quenzler Image caption, Russell Brand giving evidence at Southwark Crown Court
 On the first day of the trial, the prosecution set out details of the alleged offences involving the six women. The prosecutor described Brand as a "sexual predator" whose "strong desire for some form of sexual contact was indiscriminate and voracious".
 The prosecutor also said Brand told police in 2023 "he has never engaged in non-consensual sexual activity".
 After hearing testimony from the complainants and several witnesses, Brand took to the stand on 28 October.
 He told the jury the allegations had been "deeply traumatic" and had a "devastating" impact on him. The 51-year-old said he believes sexual consent is "fundamental".
 In his closing speech, Brand's defence barrister said there was "no evidence he is some sort of psychopath who rapes people and thinks it's normal".
